findings.title: Corpus-backed storage drops debouncing and write serialization
findings.desc: Unlike `createDebouncedLocalStorage`, the CorpusFS-backed `setItem` writes the whole persist blob on *every* `set()` (i.e. every keystroke) with no debounce and no queue, so overlapping async `writeFile` calls to the same OPFS file race; OPFS `createWritable()` takes an exclusive lock, so concurrent writes will reject with `NoModificationAllowedError` (mapped to `{kind:"io"}`) and/or land out of order, silently losing state.

findings.title: Typed CorpusErrors at the store seam become unhandled promise rejections
findings.desc: `getItem`/`setItem`/`removeItem` propagate `CorpusError` (quota, unavailable, io) but zustand's persist does not await/handle `setItem`, so a quota failure on the corpus path surfaces as an unhandled rejection with no UI and no log — a *more* silent degradation than the `console.warn` the module's own header criticizes.

findings.title: "Dev-only" flag has no dev guard
findings.desc: The doc comment and CLAUDE.md both state the flag is "DEV-ONLY", but `isCorpusEnabled()` honors `NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS=1` in production builds and the `corpus-fs-enabled` localStorage key in any browser; given enabling it means starting from an empty corpus with no migration, the missing `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"` check makes the claim misleading and the footgun real.

findings.title: Fail-loud manifest codec silently drops malformed array entries
findings.desc: `raw.sources.filter(isObject)`, `raw.artifacts.filter(isObject)` and `customTypeIds.filter(typeof x === "string")` discard non-conforming entries instead of failing, so a partially corrupted `workspace.json` parses "successfully" with fewer sources/artifacts — exactly the "masquerades as no work / masks data loss" outcome the header says parsing must prevent. `createdAt`/`updatedAt` are likewise silently defaulted to `now`.

findings.title: Slug sanitization can collide distinct workspace titles
findings.desc: `workspaceSlug` collapses unsafe runs and lowercases, so "a/b", "a-b" and "A B" all map to `a-b`, and there is no collision/uniqueness handling at the only sanctioned source of workspace paths — two workspaces would silently share one folder in S4.

findings.title: Comment claims a copy that the code does not make
findings.desc: The comment "Pass a fresh ArrayBuffer view; some implementations dislike shared buffers" sits above `await w.write(bytes)`, which passes the caller's array directly — either copy the bytes or delete the comment.

findings.title: `finally { await w.close() }` can mask the quota error it is supposed to reify
findings.desc: Real OPFS surfaces quota failures on `write()`/`close()`; if `write()` rejects, the unconditional `await w.close()` in `finally` will typically reject too (errored/closed stream) and that second error replaces the original, so the failure is mapped to `{kind:"io"}` instead of `{kind:"quota-exceeded"}`. The G7 test only stubs `createWritable()` throwing, so this realistic path is untested — consider `abort()`/try-catching the close and preserving the first error.

findings.title: Corpus-backed storage drops the 300ms debounce and serialization of writes
findings.desc: The localStorage path deliberately debounces "to avoid JSON.stringify on every keystroke", but `createCorpusBackedStorage` writes the whole persist blob to OPFS on every `set()` with no debounce and no write queue, so overlapping `createWritable()` calls on the same file can interleave (out-of-order last-write, or `NoModificationAllowedError`) and every keystroke triggers a full serialize+write.

findings.title: `process.env?.NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS` may not be statically inlined in client bundles
findings.desc: Next.js replaces the literal member expression `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_X`; writing it with optional chaining risks the substitution not matching, leaving `process.env` undefined in the browser and making the documented `NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS=1` enable path silently inert (only the localStorage path would work).

findings.title: Fail-loud contract is violated for malformed array entries
findings.desc: `raw.sources.filter(isObject)` and `customTypeIds.filter(typeof === "string")` silently discard non-object/non-string entries, and `createdAt`/`updatedAt` silently default to `now`, which is exactly the "silent partial default that masks data loss" the file header and G11 claim to forbid.

findings.title: Fake and OPFS diverge on empty directories, weakening the LSP claim
findings.desc: Directories are implicit in the fake, so after `rm` of the last file in a dir the parent `readdir` no longer lists it, whereas OPFS keeps the now-empty directory entry; the shared contract suite doesn't cover this, so a consumer relying on `readdir` semantics can pass in CI and fail against real OPFS.

findings.title: Corpus-backed storage has no debounce and no write serialization
findings.desc: Unlike the localStorage adapter (300ms debounce), `createCorpusBackedStorage` issues an OPFS `writeFile` on every zustand `setItem` (i.e. every keystroke-driven state change), and because the writes are async and unserialized, two overlapping `createWritable/write/close` cycles can complete out of order and persist a stale blob.

findings.title: Flag is documented "DEV-ONLY" but nothing enforces it
findings.desc: `isCorpusEnabled()` returns true whenever `NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS=1`, including in a production build; since S1 ships no migration, a deploy with that env var set silently starts users from an empty corpus and abandons their localStorage work. Add a `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"` guard to match the documented contract.

findings.title: Quota detection depends on `instanceof DOMException`
findings.desc: Per the newer WHATWG spec `QuotaExceededError` is its own `Error` subclass rather than a `DOMException`, so on browsers shipping that change a real OPFS quota failure would be misclassified as `{kind:"io"}`; matching on `name` (with a duck-typed check) is more robust, and the unit test's hand-built `DOMException` hides this.

findings.title: "Fail-loud" parser silently drops malformed array entries
findings.desc: `raw.sources.filter(isObject)`, `raw.artifacts.filter(isObject)` and `customTypeIds.filter(typeof x === "string")` discard non-conforming entries without error, so a partially corrupted manifest parses "successfully" with fewer sources/artifacts — exactly the silent data-loss masking the header claims to prevent.

findings.title: `close()` in `finally` can mask the original write error
findings.desc: If `w.write(bytes)` rejects (e.g. quota) and the subsequent `await w.close()` also throws, the close error replaces the write error, so the failure is reified as `{kind:"io"}` instead of `quota-exceeded`.
